questions.q: How far ahead should I book?
questions.a: Summer Saturdays go a year or more ahead. Fridays, Sundays and winter weddings, often a few months. Check your date on the cover.
A £150 booking fee, which comes off your total. Until then a date is only pencilled.

questions.q: When should I have my trial?
questions.a: Between six months and four weeks before. Your trial page works the dates out from your wedding.
Worked back from your ceremony: everyone else first, you last, with fifteen minutes spare. Before 7am there's an early-start fee.
Yes, by the hour until the speeches. Most brides take the touch-up kit instead.

questions.q: What if I have sensitive skin or allergies?
questions.a: Tell me when you book. I patch test lash glue at your trial and bring products you've used.
Free within three miles of Headingley; across Yorkshire by zone. Abroad, travel days are quoted.

guides.title: Small weddings

guides.intro: Registry offices, weekdays, the two of you.

photo.alt: A bride glancing back under a lace veil, bare skin and a nude lip

blocks.heading: Smaller, not less
blocks.body:
The same packages and the same trial as any wedding. What changes is the morning: fewer people in the chair, an easier start, and weekday dates that are free far longer than Saturdays.

For a registry office I come to wherever you're getting ready, or meet you at the studio if it's on your way.

blocks.heading: Two of you, worked out
blocks.text: Makeup for you with your trial, and hair for one other, before an 11am registry office.
blocks.note: Travel is added by postcode; free within three miles of Headingley.
